2522.text: But the end of all things is at hand: be ye therefore sober, and watch unto prayer.

2523.text: And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.

2524.text: Use hospitality one to another without grudging.

2525.text: As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.

2526.text: If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God; if any man minister, let him do it as of the ability which God giveth: that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be praise and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.

2527.text: Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you:

2528.text: But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ’s sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.

2529.text: If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.

2530.text: But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters.

2531.text: Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf.

2532.text: For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God: and if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God?

2533.text: And if the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?

2534.text: Wherefore let them that suffer according to the will of God commit the keeping of their souls to him in well doing, as unto a faithful Creator.

2535.text: The elders which are among you I exhort, who am also an elder, and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a partaker of the glory that shall be revealed:

2536.text: Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind;

2537.text: Neither as being lords over God’s heritage, but being ensamples to the flock.

2538.text: And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away.

2539.text: Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.

2540.text: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time:

2541.text: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

2542.text: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour:

2543.text: Whom resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.

2544.text: But the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.

2545.text: To him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.

2546.text: By Silvanus, a faithful brother unto you, as I suppose, I have written briefly, exhorting, and testifying that this is the true grace of God wherein ye stand.

2547.text: The church that is at Babylon, elected together with you, saluteth you; and so doth Marcus my son.

2548.text: Greet ye one another with a kiss of charity. Peace be with you all that are in Christ Jesus. Amen.

2549.text: Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, to them that have obtained like precious faith with us through the righteousness of God and our Saviour Jesus Christ:

2550.text: Grace and peace be multiplied unto you through the knowledge of God, and of Jesus our Lord,

2551.text: According as his divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue:

2552.text: Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.

2553.text: And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge;

2554.text: And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness;

2555.text: And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity.

2556.text: For if these things be in you, and abound, they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

2557.text: But he that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.

2558.text: Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall:

2559.text: For so an entrance shall be ministered unto you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.

2560.text: Wherefore I will not be negligent to put you always in remembrance of these things, though ye know them, and be established in the present truth.

2561.text: Yea, I think it meet, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance;

2562.text: Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me.

2563.text: Moreover I will endeavour that ye may be able after my decease to have these things always in remembrance.

2564.text: For we have not followed cunningly devised fables, when we made known unto you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but were eyewitnesses of his majesty.

2565.text: For he received from God the Father honour and glory, when there came such a voice to him from the excellent glory, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

2566.text: And this voice which came from heaven we heard, when we were with him in the holy mount.

2567.text: We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts:

2568.text: Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation.

2569.text: For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.

2570.text: But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction.

2571.text: And many shall follow their pernicious ways; by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of.

2572.text: And through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you: whose judgment now of a long time lingereth not, and their damnation slumbereth not.

2573.text: For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;

2574.text: And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly;

2575.text: And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly;

2576.text: And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked:

2577.text: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)

2578.text: The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished:

2579.text: But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.

2580.text: Whereas angels, which are greater in power and might, bring not railing accusation against them before the Lord.

2581.text: But these, as natural brute beasts, made to be taken and destroyed, speak evil of the things that they understand not; and shall utterly perish in their own corruption;

2582.text: And shall receive the reward of unrighteousness, as they that count it pleasure to riot in the day time. Spots they are and blemishes, sporting themselves with their own deceivings while they feast with you;

2583.text: Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls: an heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children:

2584.text: Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness;

2585.text: But was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man’s voice forbad the madness of the prophet.

2586.text: These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever.

2587.text: For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error.

2588.text: While they promise them liberty, they themselves are the servants of corruption: for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage.

2589.text: For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning.

2590.text: For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them.

2591.text: But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.

2592.text: This second epistle, beloved, I now write unto you; in both which I stir up your pure minds by way of remembrance:

2593.text: That ye may be mindful of the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets, and of the commandment of us the apostles of the Lord and Saviour:

2594.text: Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts,

2595.text: And saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.

2596.text: For this they willingly are ignorant of, that by the word of God the heavens were of old, and the earth standing out of the water and in the water:

2597.text: Whereby the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished:

2598.text: But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.

2599.text: But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.

2600.text: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

2601.text: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up.

2602.text: Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness,

2603.text: Looking for and hasting unto the coming of the day of God, wherein the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat?

2604.text: Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.

2605.text: Wherefore, beloved, seeing that ye look for such things, be diligent that ye may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless.

2606.text: And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you;

2607.text: As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.

2608.text: Ye therefore, beloved, seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness.

2609.text: But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and for ever. Amen.

2610.text: That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life;

2611.text: (For the life was manifested, and we have seen it, and bear witness, and shew unto you that eternal life, which was with the Father, and was manifested unto us;)

2612.text: That which we have seen and heard declare we unto you, that ye also may have fellowship with us: and truly our fellowship is with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ.

2613.text: And these things write we unto you, that your joy may be full.

2614.text: This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.

2615.text: If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not the truth:

2616.text: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.

2617.text: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.

2618.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

2619.text: If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.

2620.text: My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not. And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous:

2621.text: And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.

2622.text: And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments.

2623.text: He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.

2624.text: But whoso keepeth his word, in him verily is the love of God perfected: hereby know we that we are in him.

2625.text: He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.

2626.text: Brethren, I write no new commandment unto you, but an old commandment which ye had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word which ye have heard from the beginning.

2627.text: Again, a new commandment I write unto you, which thing is true in him and in you: because the darkness is past, and the true light now shineth.

2628.text: He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now.

2629.text: He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him.

2630.text: But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes.

2631.text: I write unto you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name’s sake.

2632.text: I write unto you, fathers, because ye have known him that is from the beginning. I write unto you, young men, because ye have overcome the wicked one. I write unto you, little children, because ye have known the Father.

2633.text: I have written unto you, fathers, because ye have known him that is from the beginning. I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one.

2634.text: Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.

2635.text: For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.

2636.text: And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.

2637.text: Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists; whereby we know that it is the last time.

2638.text: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.

2639.text: But ye have an unction from the Holy One, and ye know all things.

2640.text: I have not written unto you because ye know not the truth, but because ye know it, and that no lie is of the truth.

2641.text: Who is a liar but he that denieth that Jesus is the Christ? He is antichrist, that denieth the Father and the Son.

2642.text: Whosoever denieth the Son, the same hath not the Father: but he that acknowledgeth the Son hath the Father also.

2643.text: Let that therefore abide in you, which ye have heard from the beginning. If that which ye have heard from the beginning shall remain in you, ye also shall continue in the Son, and in the Father.

2644.text: And this is the promise that he hath promised us, even eternal life.

2645.text: These things have I written unto you concerning them that seduce you.

2646.text: But the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you, and ye need not that any man teach you: but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things, and is truth, and is no lie, and even as it hath taught you, ye shall abide in him.

2647.text: And now, little children, abide in him; that, when he shall appear, we may have confidence, and not be ashamed before him at his coming.

2648.text: If ye know that he is righteous, ye know that every one that doeth righteousness is born of him.

2649.text: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.

2650.text: Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.

2651.text: And every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure.

2652.text: Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.

2653.text: And ye know that he was manifested to take away our sins; and in him is no sin.

2654.text: Whosoever abideth in him sinneth not: whosoever sinneth hath not seen him, neither known him.

2655.text: Little children, let no man deceive you: he that doeth righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous.

2656.text: He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.

2657.text: Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God.

2658.text: In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother.

2659.text: For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.

2660.text: Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.

2661.text: Marvel not, my brethren, if the world hate you.

2662.text: We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not his brother abideth in death.

2663.text: Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.

2664.text: Hereby perceive we the love of God, because he laid down his life for us: and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren.

2665.text: But whoso hath this world’s good, and seeth his brother have need, and shutteth up his bowels of compassion from him, how dwelleth the love of God in him?

2666.text: My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth.

2667.text: And hereby we know that we are of the truth, and shall assure our hearts before him.

2668.text: For if our heart condemn us, God is greater than our heart, and knoweth all things.

2669.text: Beloved, if our heart condemn us not, then have we confidence toward God.

2670.text: And whatsoever we ask, we receive of him, because we keep his commandments, and do those things that are pleasing in his sight.

2671.text: And this is his commandment, That we should believe on the name of his Son Jesus Christ, and love one another, as he gave us commandment.

2672.text: And he that keepeth his commandments dwelleth in him, and he in him. And hereby we know that he abideth in us, by the Spirit which he hath given us.

2673.text: Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world.

2674.text: Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God:

2675.text: And every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come; and even now already is it in the world.

2676.text: Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world.

2677.text: They are of the world: therefore speak they of the world, and the world heareth them.

2678.text: We are of God: he that knoweth God heareth us; he that is not of God heareth not us. Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.

2679.text: Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God.

2680.text: He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.

2681.text: In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him.

2682.text: Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.

2683.text: Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another.

2684.text: No man hath seen God at any time. If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us.

2685.text: Hereby know we that we dwell in him, and he in us, because he hath given us of his Spirit.

2686.text: And we have seen and do testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world.

2687.text: Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God dwelleth in him, and he in God.

2688.text: And we have known and believed the love that God hath to us. God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him.

2689.text: Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment: because as he is, so are we in this world.

2690.text: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.

2691.text: We love him, because he first loved us.

2692.text: If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?

2693.text: And this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also.

2694.text: Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him.

2695.text: By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God, and keep his commandments.

2696.text: For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.

2697.text: For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.

2698.text: Who is he that overcometh the world, but he that believeth that Jesus is the Son of God?

2699.text: This is he that came by water and blood, even Jesus Christ; not by water only, but by water and blood. And it is the Spirit that beareth witness, because the Spirit is truth.

2700.text: For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.

2701.text: And there are three that bear witness in earth, the spirit, and the water, and the blood: and these three agree in one.

2702.text: If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater: for this is the witness of God which he hath testified of his Son.

2703.text: He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.

2704.text: And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.

2705.text: He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.

2706.text: These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God.

2707.text: And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us:

2708.text: And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him.

2709.text: If any man see his brother sin a sin which is not unto death, he shall ask, and he shall give him life for them that sin not unto death. There is a sin unto death: I do not say that he shall pray for it.

2710.text: All unrighteousness is sin: and there is a sin not unto death.

2711.text: We know that whosoever is born of God sinneth not; but he that is begotten of God keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not.

2712.text: And we know that we are of God, and the whole world lieth in wickedness.

2713.text: And we know that the Son of God is come, and hath given us an understanding, that we may know him that is true, and we are in him that is true, even in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life.

2714.text: Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Amen.

2715.text: The elder unto the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth; and not I only, but also all they that have known the truth;

2716.text: For the truth’s sake, which dwelleth in us, and shall be with us for ever.

2717.text: Grace be with you, mercy, and peace, from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.

2718.text: I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children walking in truth, as we have received a commandment from the Father.

2719.text: And now I beseech thee, lady, not as though I wrote a new commandment unto thee, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another.

2720.text: And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.

2721.text: For many deceivers are entered into the world, who confess not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh. This is a deceiver and an antichrist.

2722.text: Look to yourselves, that we lose not those things which we have wrought, but that we receive a full reward.

2723.text: Whosoever transgresseth, and abideth not in the doctrine of Christ, hath not God. He that abideth in the doctrine of Christ, he hath both the Father and the Son.

2724.text: If there come any unto you, and bring not this doctrine, receive him not into your house, neither bid him God speed:

2725.text: For he that biddeth him God speed is partaker of his evil deeds.

2726.text: Having many things to write unto you, I would not write with paper and ink: but I trust to come unto you, and speak face to face, that our joy may be full.

2727.text: The children of thy elect sister greet thee. Amen.

2728.text: The elder unto the wellbeloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth.

2729.text: Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth.

2730.text: For I rejoiced greatly, when the brethren came and testified of the truth that is in thee, even as thou walkest in the truth.

2731.text: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.

2732.text: Beloved, thou doest faithfully whatsoever thou doest to the brethren, and to strangers;

2733.text: Which have borne witness of thy charity before the church: whom if thou bring forward on their journey after a godly sort, thou shalt do well:

2734.text: Because that for his name’s sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles.

2735.text: We therefore ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth.

2736.text: I wrote unto the church: but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.

2737.text: Wherefore, if I come, I will remember his deeds which he doeth, prating against us with malicious words: and not content therewith, neither doth he himself receive the brethren, and forbiddeth them that would, and casteth them out of the church.

2738.text: Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God.

2739.text: Demetrius hath good report of all men, and of the truth itself: yea, and we also bear record; and ye know that our record is true.

2740.text: I had many things to write, but I will not with ink and pen write unto thee:

2741.text: But I trust I shall shortly see thee, and we shall speak face to face. Peace be to thee. Our friends salute thee. Greet the friends by name.

2742.text: Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to them that are sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called:

2743.text: Mercy unto you, and peace, and love, be multiplied.

2744.text: Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints.

2745.text: For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ.

2746.text: I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not.

2747.text: And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.

2748.text: Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.

2749.text: Likewise also these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities.

2750.text: Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee.

2751.text: But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves.

2752.text: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.

2753.text: These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots;

2754.text: Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever.

2755.text: And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints,

2756.text: To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.

2757.text: These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts; and their mouth speaketh great swelling words, having men’s persons in admiration because of advantage.

2758.text: But, beloved, remember ye the words which were spoken before of the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ;

2759.text: How that they told you there should be mockers in the last time, who should walk after their own ungodly lusts.

2760.text: These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit.

2761.text: But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost,

2762.text: Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life.

2763.text: And of some have compassion, making a difference:

2764.text: And others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.

2765.text: Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy,

2766.text: To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen.

2767.text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart for the Good News of God,

2768.text: which he promised before through his prophets in the holy Scriptures,

2769.text: concerning his Son, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh,

2770.text: who was declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,

2771.text: through whom we received grace and the office of apostle, for obedience of faith among all the nations, for his name's sake;

2772.text: among whom you are also called to belong to Jesus Christ;

2773.text: to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

2774.text: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, that your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.

2775.text: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Good News of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you always in my prayers,

2776.text: requesting, if by any means now at last I may be prospered by the will of God to come to you.

2777.text: For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, to the end that you may be established;

2778.text: that is, that I with you may be encouraged in you, each of us by the other's faith, both yours and mine.

2779.text: Now I do not desire to have you unaware, brothers, that I often planned to come to you, and was hindered so far, that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among the rest of the Gentiles.

2780.text: I am debtor both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to the wise and to the foolish.

2781.text: So, as much as is in me, I am eager to proclaim the Good News to you also who are in Rome.

2782.text: For I am not ashamed of the Good News, for it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes; for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.

2783.text: For in it is revealed God's righteousness from faith to faith. As it is written, "But the righteous shall live by faith."

2784.text: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,

2785.text: because that which is known of God is revealed in them, for God revealed it to them.

2786.text: For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divine nature; that they may be without excuse.

2787.text: Because, knowing God, they did not glorify him as God, neither gave thanks, but became vain in their reasoning, and their senseless heart was darkened.

2788.text: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

2789.text: and traded the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, and four-footed animals, and creeping things.

2790.text: Therefore God also abandoned them in the lusts of their hearts to uncleanness, that their bodies should be dishonored among themselves,

2791.text: who exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.

2792.text: For this reason, God abandoned them to their degrading passions. For their women changed the natural function into that which is against nature.

2793.text: Likewise also the men, leaving the natural function of the woman, burned in their lust toward one another, men doing what is inappropriate with men, and receiving in themselves the due penalty of their error.

2794.text: Even as they refused to have God in their knowledge, God abandoned them to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not fitting;

2795.text: being filled with all unrighteousness, sexual immorality, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil habits, secret slanderers,

2796.text: backbiters, hateful to God, insolent, haughty, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,

2797.text: without understanding, covenant breakers, without natural affection, unmerciful;

2798.text: who, knowing the ordinance of God, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but also approve of those who practice them.

2799.text: Therefore you are without excuse, O man, whoever you are who judge. For in that which you judge another, you condemn yourself. For you who judge practice the same things.

2800.text: We know that the judgment of God is according to truth against those who practice such things.

2801.text: Do you think this, O man who judges those who practice such things, and do the same, that you will escape the judgment of God?

2802.text: Or do you despise the riches of his goodness, forbearance, and patience, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?

2803.text: But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart you are treasuring up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath, revelation, and of the righteous judgment of God;

2804.text: who "will pay back to everyone according to their works:"

2805.text: to those who by patience in well-doing seek for glory, honor, and incorruptibility, eternal life;

2806.text: but to those who are self-seeking, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, will be wrath and indignation,

2807.text: oppression and anguish, on every soul of man who works evil, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

2808.text: But glory, honor, and peace go to every man who works good, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

2809.text: For there is no partiality with God.

2810.text: For as many as have sinned without law will also perish without the law. As many as have sinned under the law will be judged by the law.

2811.text: For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but the doers of the law will be justified

2812.text: (for when Gentiles who do not have the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves,

2813.text: in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their thoughts among themselves accusing or else excusing them)

2814.text: in the day when God will judge the secrets of men, according to my Good News, by Christ Jesus.

2815.text: But if you call yourself a Jew, and rest on the law, and glory in God,

2816.text: and know his will, and approve the things that are excellent, being instructed out of the law,

2817.text: and are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light to those who are in darkness,

2818.text: a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of children, having in the law the form of knowledge and of the truth.

2819.text: You therefore who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who proclaim that a man should not steal, do you steal?

2820.text: You who say a man should not commit adultery. Do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?

2821.text: You who glory in the law, through your disobedience of the law do you dishonor God?

2822.text: For "the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you," just as it is written.

2823.text: For circumcision indeed profits, if you are a doer of the law, but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.

2824.text: If therefore the uncircumcised keep the ordinances of the law, won't his uncircumcision be accounted as circumcision?

2825.text: Won't the uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfills the law, judge you, who with the letter and circumcision are a transgressor of the law?

2826.text: For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh;

2827.text: but he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit not in the letter; whose praise is not from men, but from God.

2828.text: Then what advantage does the Jew have? Or what is the profit of circumcision?

2829.text: Much in every way! Because first of all, they were entrusted with the oracles of God.

2830.text: For what if some were without faith? Will their lack of faith nullify the faithfulness of God?

2831.text: May it never be! Yes, let God be found true, but every man a liar. As it is written, "That you might be justified in your words, and might prevail when you come into judgment."

2832.text: But if our unrighteousness commends the righteousness of God, what will we say? Is God unrighteous who inflicts wrath? I speak like men do.

2833.text: May it never be! For then how will God judge the world?

2834.text: For if the truth of God through my lie abounded to his glory, why am I also still judged as a sinner?

2835.text: Why not (as we are slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say), "Let us do evil, that good may come?" Those who say so are justly condemned.

2836.text: What then? Are we better than they? No, in no way. For we previously warned both Jews and Greeks, that they are all under sin.

2837.text: As it is written, "There is no one righteous; no, not one.

2838.text: There is no one who understands. There is no one who seeks after God.

2839.text: They have all turned aside. They have together become unprofitable. There is no one who does good, no, not, so much as one."

2840.text: "Their throat is an open tomb. With their tongues they have used deceit." "The poison of vipers is under their lips;"

2841.text: "Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness."

2842.text: "Their feet are swift to shed blood.

2843.text: Destruction and misery are in their ways.

2844.text: The way of peace, they have not known."

2845.text: "There is no fear of God before their eyes."

2846.text: Now we know that whatever things the law says, it speaks to those who are under the law, that every mouth may be closed, and all the world may be brought under the judgment of God.

2847.text: Because by the works of the law, no flesh will be justified in his sight. For through the law comes the knowledge of sin.

2848.text: But now apart from the law, a righteousness of God has been revealed, being testified by the Law and the Prophets;

2849.text: even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ to all those who believe. For there is no distinction,

2850.text: for all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God;

2851.text: being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus;

2852.text: whom God set forth to be an atoning sacrifice, through faith in his blood, for a demonstration of his righteousness through the passing over of prior sins, in God's forbearance;

2853.text: to demonstrate his righteousness at this present time; that he might himself be just, and the justifier of him who has faith in Jesus.

2854.text: Where then is the boasting? It is excluded. By what manner of law? Of works? No, but by a law of faith.

2855.text: We maintain therefore that a man is justified by faith apart from the works of the law.

2856.text: Or is God the God of Jews only? Is not he the God of Gentiles also? Yes, of Gentiles also,

2857.text: since indeed there is one God who will justify the circumcised by faith, and the uncircumcised through faith.

2858.text: Do we then nullify the law through faith? May it never be! No, we establish the law.

2859.text: What then will we say that Abraham, our forefather, has found according to the flesh?

2860.text: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about, but not toward God.

2861.text: For what does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness."

2862.text: Now to him who works, the reward is not counted as grace, but as debt.

2863.text: But to him who does not work, but believes in him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is accounted for righteousness.

2864.text: Even as David also pronounces blessing on the man to whom God counts righteousness apart from works,

2865.text: "Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, whose sins are covered.

2866.text: Blessed is the man whom the Lord will by no means charge with sin."

2867.text: Is this blessing then pronounced on the circumcised, or on the uncircumcised also? For we say that faith was accounted to Abraham for righteousness.

2868.text: How then was it counted? When he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

2869.text: He received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had while he was in uncircumcision, that he might be the father of all those who believe, though they be in uncircumcision, that righteousness might also be accounted to them.

2870.text: The father of circumcision to those who not only are of the circumcision, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had in uncircumcision.

2871.text: For the promise to Abraham and to his seed that he should be heir of the world was not through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.

2872.text: For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith is made void, and the promise is made of no effect.

2873.text: For the law works wrath, for where there is no law, neither is there disobedience.

2874.text: For this cause it is of faith, that it may be according to grace, to the end that the promise may be sure to all the seed, not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all.

2875.text: As it is written, "I have made you a father of many nations." This is in the presence of him whom he believed: God, who gives life to the dead, and calls the things that are not, as though they were.

2876.text: Who in hope believed against hope, to the end that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken, "So will your seed be."

2877.text: Without being weakened in faith, he considered his own body, already having been worn out, (he being about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah's womb.

2878.text: Yet, looking to the promise of God, he did not waver through unbelief, but grew strong through faith, giving glory to God,

2879.text: and being fully assured that what he had promised, he was able also to perform.

2880.text: Therefore it also was "reckoned to him for righteousness."

2881.text: Now it was not written that it was accounted to him for his sake alone,

2882.text: but for our sake also, to whom it will be accounted, who believe in him who raised Jesus, our Lord, from the dead,

2883.text: who was delivered up for our trespasses, and was raised for our justification.

2884.text: Being therefore justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ;

2885.text: through whom we also have our access by faith into this grace in which we stand. We rejoice in hope of the glory of God.

2886.text: Not only this, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering works perseverance;

2887.text: and perseverance, proven character; and proven character, hope:

2888.text: and hope does not disappoint us, because God's love has been poured out into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.

2889.text: For while we were yet weak, at the right time Christ died for the ungodly.

2890.text: For rarely does one die for the righteous. Yet perhaps for a good person someone might dare to die.

2891.text: But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

2892.text: Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we will be saved from God's wrath through him.

2893.text: For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we will be saved by his life.

2894.text: Not only so, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.

2895.text: Therefore, as sin entered into the world through one man, and death through sin; and so death passed to all men, because all sinned.

2896.text: For until the law, sin was in the world; but sin is not charged when there is no law.

2897.text: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those whose sins weren't like Adam's disobedience, who is a foreshadowing of him who was to come.

2898.text: But the free gift is not like the trespass. For if by the trespass of the one the many died, much more did the grace of God, and the gift by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many.

2899.text: The gift is not as through one who sinned: for the judgment came by one to condemnation, but the free gift came of many trespasses to justification.

2900.text: For if by the trespass of the one, death reigned through the one; so much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one, Jesus Christ.

2901.text: So then as through one trespass, all men were condemned; even so through one act of righteousness, all men were justified to life.

2902.text: For as through the one man's disobedience many were made sinners, even so through the obedience of the one, many will be made righteous.

2903.text: The law came in besides, that the trespass might abound; but where sin abounded, grace abounded more exceedingly;

2904.text: that as sin reigned in death, even so grace might reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

2905.text: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?

2906.text: May it never be! We who died to sin, how could we live in it any longer?

2907.text: Or do you not know that all we who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?

2908.text: We were buried therefore with him through baptism to death, that just like Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.

2909.text: For if we have become united with him in the likeness of his death, we will also be part of his resurrection;

2910.text: knowing this, that our old man was crucified with him, that the body of sin might be done away with, so that we would no longer be in bondage to sin.

2911.text: For he who has died has been freed from sin.

2912.text: But if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him;

2913.text: knowing that Christ, being raised from the dead, dies no more. Death no more has dominion over him!

2914.text: For the death that he died, he died to sin one time; but the life that he lives, he lives to God.

2915.text: Thus consider yourselves also to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.

2916.text: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body, that you should obey it in its lusts.

2917.text: Neither present your members to sin as instruments of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God, as alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God.

2918.text: For sin will not have dominion over you. For you are not under law, but under grace.

2919.text: What then? Shall we sin, because we are not under law, but under grace? May it never be!

2920.text: Do you not know that to whom you present yourselves as servants to obedience, his servants you are whom you obey; whether of sin to death, or of obedience to righteousness?

2921.text: But thanks be to God, that, whereas you were bondservants of sin, you became obedient from the heart to that form of teaching whereunto you were delivered.

2922.text: Being made free from sin, you became bondservants of righteousness.

2923.text: I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh, for as you presented your members as servants to uncleanness and to wickedness upon wickedness, even so now present your members as servants to righteousness for sanctification.

2924.text: For when you were servants of sin, you were free in regard to righteousness.

2925.text: What fruit then did you have at that time in the things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death.

2926.text: But now, being made free from sin, and having become servants of God, you have your fruit of sanctification, and the result of eternal life.

2927.text: For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

2928.text: Or do you not know, brothers (for I speak to men who know the law), that the law has dominion over a man for as long as he lives?

2929.text: For the woman that has a husband is bound by law to the husband while he lives, but if the husband dies, she is discharged from the law of the husband.

2930.text: So then if, while the husband lives, she is joined to another man, she would be called an adulteress. But if the husband dies, she is free from the law, so that she is no adulteress, though she is joined to another man.

2931.text: Therefore, my brothers, you also were made dead to the law through the body of Christ, that you would be joined to another, to him who was raised from the dead, that we might bring forth fruit to God.

2932.text: For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions which were through the law, worked in our members to bring forth fruit to death.

2933.text: But now we have been discharged from the law, having died to that in which we were held; so that we serve in newness of the spirit, and not in oldness of the letter.

2934.text: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? May it never be! However, I would not have known sin, except through the law. For I would not have known coveting, unless the law had said, "You shall not covet."

2935.text: But sin, finding occasion through the commandment, produced in me all kinds of coveting. For apart from the law, sin is dead.

2936.text: I was alive apart from the law once, but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died.

2937.text: The commandment, which was for life, this I found to be for death;

2938.text: for sin, finding occasion through the commandment, deceived me, and through it killed me.

2939.text: Therefore the law indeed is holy, and the commandment holy, and righteous, and good.

2940.text: Did then that which is good become death to me? May it never be! But sin, that it might be shown to be sin, by working death to me through that which is good; that through the commandment sin might become exceeding sinful.

2941.text: For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am fleshly, sold under sin.

2942.text: For I do not know what I am doing. For I do not practice what I desire to do; but what I hate, that I do.

2943.text: But if what I do not desire, that I do, I consent to the law that it is good.

2944.text: So now it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwells in me.

2945.text: For I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, dwells no good thing. For desire is present with me, but to do that which is good is not.

2946.text: For the good which I desire, I do not do; but the evil which I do not desire, that I practice.

2947.text: But if what I do not desire, that I do, it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwells in me.

2948.text: I find then the law, that, to me, while I desire to do good, evil is present.

2949.text: For I delight in God's law after the inward man,

2950.text: but I see a different law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity under the law of sin which is in my members.

2951.text: What a wretched man I am! Who will deliver me out of the body of this death?

2952.text: Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ, our Lord! So then with the mind, I myself serve God's law, but with the flesh, the sin's law.

2953.text: There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus.

2954.text: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made you free from the law of sin and of death.

2955.text: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God did, sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, he condemned sin in the flesh;

2956.text: that the ordinance of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

2957.text: For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those who live according to the Spirit, the things of the Spirit.

2958.text: For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace;

2959.text: because the mind of the flesh is hostile towards God; for it is not subject to God's law, neither indeed can it be.

2960.text: Those who are in the flesh cannot please God.

2961.text: But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if it is so that the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if any man does not have the Spirit of Christ, he is not his.

2962.text: If Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit is alive because of righteousness.

2963.text: But if the Spirit of him who raised up Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised up Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you.

2964.text: So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh.

2965.text: For if you live after the flesh, you must die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.

2966.text: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God.

2967.text: For you did not receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, "Abba! Father!"

2968.text: The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God;

2969.text: and if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint heirs with Christ; if indeed we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified with him.

2970.text: For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which will be revealed toward us.

2971.text: For the creation waits with eager expectation for the children of God to be revealed.

2972.text: For the creation was subjected to vanity, not of its own will, but because of him who subjected it, in hope

2973.text: that the creation itself also will be delivered from the bondage of decay into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.

2974.text: For we know that the whole creation groans and travails in pain together until now.

2975.text: Not only so, but ourselves also, who have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for adoption, the redemption of our body.

2976.text: For we were saved in hope, but hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for that which he sees?

2977.text: But if we hope for that which we do not see, we wait for it with patience.

2978.text: In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we do not know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.

2979.text: He who searches the hearts knows what is on the Spirit's mind, because he makes intercession for the saints according to God.

2980.text: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, to those who are called according to his purpose.

2981.text: For whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers.

2982.text: Whom he predestined, those he also called. Whom he called, those he also justified. Whom he justified, those he also glorified.

2983.text: What then shall we say about these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?

2984.text: He who did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how would he not also with him freely give us all things?

2985.text: Who could bring a charge against God's chosen ones? It is God who justifies.

2986.text: Who is he who condemns? It is Christ who died, yes rather, who was raised from the dead, who is at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us.

2987.text: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Could oppression, or anguish, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?

2988.text: Even as it is written, "For your sake we are killed all day long. We were accounted as sheep for the slaughter."

2989.text: No, in all these things, we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.

2990.text: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,

2991.text: nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

2992.text: I tell the truth in Christ. I am not lying, my conscience testifying with me in the Holy Spirit,

2993.text: that I have great sorrow and unceasing pain in my heart.

2994.text: For I could wish that I myself were accursed from Christ for my brothers' sake, my relatives according to the flesh,

2995.text: who are Israelites; whose is the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the service, and the promises;

2996.text: of whom are the fathers, and from whom is Christ as concerning the flesh, who is over all, God, blessed forever. Amen.

2997.text: But it is not as though the word of God has come to nothing. For they are not all Israel, that are of Israel.

2998.text: Neither, because they are Abraham's seed, are they all children. But, "In Isaac will your seed be called."

2999.text: That is, it is not the children of the flesh who are children of God, but the children of the promise are counted as a seed.

3000.text: For this is a word of promise, "At the appointed time I will come, and Sarah will have a son."

3001.text: Not only so, but Rebekah also conceived by one, by our father Isaac.

3002.text: For being not yet born, neither having done anything good or bad, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him who calls,

3003.text: it was said to her, "The elder will serve the younger."

3004.text: Even as it is written, "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated."

3005.text: What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? May it never be!

3006.text: For he said to Moses, "I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion."

3007.text: So then it is not of him who wills, nor of him who runs, but of God who has mercy.

3008.text: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh, "For this very purpose I caused you to be raised up, that I might show in you my power, and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth."

3009.text: So then, he has mercy on whom he desires, and he hardens whom he desires.

3010.text: You will say then to me, "Why does he still find fault? For who withstands his will?"

3011.text: But indeed, O man, who are you to reply against God? Will the thing formed ask him who formed it, "Why did you make me like this?"

3012.text: Or hasn't the potter a right over the clay, from the same lump to make one part a vessel for honor, and another for dishonor?

3013.text: What if God, willing to show his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much patience vessels of wrath made for destruction,

3014.text: and that he might make known the riches of his glory on vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory,

3015.text: us, whom he also called, not from the Jews only, but also from the Gentiles?

3016.text: As he says also in Hosea, "I will call them 'my people,' which were not my people; and her 'beloved,' who was not beloved."

3017.text: "It will be that in the place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' There they will be called 'children of the living God.'"

3018.text: Isaiah cries out concerning Israel, "If the number of the sons of Israel are as the sand of the sea, it is the remnant who will be saved;

3019.text: for the Lord will fulfill his word completely and without delay upon the earth."

3020.text: As Isaiah has said before, "Unless the Lord of hosts had left us a seed, we would have become like Sodom, and would have been made like Gomorrah."

3021.text: What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, who did not follow after righteousness, attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith;

3022.text: but Israel, following after a law of righteousness, did not arrive at that law.

3023.text: Why? Because they did not seek it by faith, but as it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone;

3024.text: even as it is written, "Behold, I lay in Zion a stumbling stone and a rock that will make them fall; and no one who believes in him will be put to shame."

3025.text: Brothers, my heart's desire and my prayer to God is for them, that they may be saved.

3026.text: For I testify about them that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.

3027.text: For being ignorant of God's righteousness, and seeking to establish their own righteousness, they did not subject themselves to the righteousness of God.

3028.text: For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes.

3029.text: For Moses writes about the righteousness of the law, "The one who does them will live by them."

3030.text: But the righteousness which is of faith says this, "Do not say in your heart, 'Who will ascend into heaven?' (that is, to bring Christ down);

3031.text: or, 'Who will descend into the abyss?' (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.)"

3032.text: But what does it say? "The word is near you, in your mouth, and in your heart;" that is, the word of faith, which we proclaim:

3033.text: that if you will confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.

3034.text: For with the heart, one believes unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.

3035.text: For the Scripture says, "Whoever believes in him will not be disappointed."

3036.text: For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; for the same Lord of all is rich to all who call on him.

3037.text: For, "Whoever will call on the name of the Lord will be saved."

3038.text: How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? How will they believe in him whom they have not heard? How will they hear without a proclaimer?

3039.text: And how will they proclaim unless they are sent? As it is written: "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring glad tidings of good things!"

3040.text: But they did not all listen to the glad news. For Isaiah says, "Lord, who has believed our report?"

3041.text: So faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.

3042.text: But I say, did they not hear? Yes, truly, "Their sound went out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world."

3043.text: But I ask, did not Israel know? First Moses says, "I will provoke you to jealousy with that which is no nation, with a nation void of understanding I will make you angry."

3044.text: Isaiah is very bold, and says, "I was found by those who did not seek me. I was revealed to those who did not ask for me."

3045.text: But as to Israel he says, "All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people."

3046.text: I ask then, did God reject his people? May it never be! For I also am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

3047.text: God did not reject his people, which he foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says about Elijah? How he pleads with God against Israel:

3048.text: "Lord, they have killed your prophets, they have broken down your altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life."

3049.text: But how does God answer him? "I have reserved for myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to Baal."

3050.text: Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.

3051.text: And if by grace, then it is no longer of works; otherwise grace is no longer grace.

3052.text: What then? That which Israel seeks for, that he did not obtain, but the chosen ones obtained it, and the rest were hardened.

3053.text: According as it is written, "God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, to this very day."

3054.text: David says, "Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, a stumbling block, and a retribution to them.

3055.text: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see. Bow down their back always."

3056.text: I ask then, did they stumble that they might fall? May it never be! But by their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.

3057.text: Now if their fall is the riches of the world, and their loss the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fullness?

3058.text: For I speak to you who are Gentiles. Since then as I am an apostle to Gentiles, I glorify my ministry;

3059.text: if by any means I may provoke to jealousy those who are my flesh, and may save some of them.

3060.text: For if the rejection of them is the reconciling of the world, what would their acceptance be, but life from the dead?

3061.text: If the first fruit is holy, so is the lump. If the root is holy, so are the branches.

3062.text: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them, and became partaker with them of the root and of the richness of the olive tree;

3063.text: do not boast over the branches. But if you boast, it is not you who support the root, but the root supports you.

3064.text: You will say then, "Branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in."

3065.text: True; by their unbelief they were broken off, and you stand by your faith. Do not be conceited, but fear;

3066.text: for if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.

3067.text: See then the goodness and severity of God. Toward those who fell, severity; but toward you, goodness, if you continue in his goodness; otherwise you also will be cut off.

3068.text: They also, if they do not continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.

3069.text: For if you were cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree, how much more will these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?

3070.text: For I do not desire you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, so that you won't be wise in your own conceits, that a partial hardening has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in,

3071.text: and so all Israel will be saved. Even as it is written, "There will come out of Zion the Deliverer, and he will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.

3072.text: This is my covenant to them, when I will take away their sins."

3073.text: Concerning the Good News, they are enemies for your sake. But concerning the election, they are beloved for the fathers' sake.

3074.text: For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.

3075.text: For as you in time past were disobedient to God, but now have obtained mercy by their disobedience,

3076.text: even so these also have now been disobedient, that by the mercy shown to you they may also obtain mercy.

3077.text: For God has shut up all to disobedience, that he might have mercy on all.

3078.text: Oh the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and the knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past tracing out!

3079.text: "For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counselor?"

3080.text: "Or who has first given to him, and it will be repaid to him again?"

3081.text: For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things. To him be the glory for ever! Amen.

3082.text: Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service.

3083.text: And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.

3084.text: For I say, through the grace that was given me, to every man who is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think reasonably, as God has apportioned to each person a measure of faith.

3085.text: For even as we have many members in one body, and all the members do not have the same function,

3086.text: so we, who are many, are one body in Christ, and individually members one of another.

3087.text: Having gifts differing according to the grace that was given to us, if prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of our faith;

3088.text: or service, let us give ourselves to service; or he who teaches, to his teaching;

3089.text: or he who exhorts, to his exhorting: he who gives, let him do it with liberality; he who rules, with diligence; he who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.

3090.text: Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor that which is evil. Cling to that which is good.

3091.text: In love of the brothers be tenderly affectionate one to another; outdo one another in showing honor;

3092.text: not lagging in diligence; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;

3093.text: rejoicing in hope; enduring in troubles; continuing steadfastly in prayer;

3094.text: contributing to the needs of the saints; given to hospitality.

3095.text: Bless those who persecute you; bless, and do not curse.

3096.text: Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.

3097.text: Be of the same mind one toward another. Do not be arrogant, but associate with the humble. Do not be wise in your own conceits.

3098.text: Repay no one evil for evil. Respect what is honorable in the sight of all men.

3099.text: If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.

3100.text: Do not seek revenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to God's wrath. For it is written, "Vengeance belongs to me; I will repay, says the Lord."

3101.text: Therefore "If your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him a drink; for in doing so, you will heap coals of fire on his head."

3102.text: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

3103.text: Let every soul be in subjection to the higher authorities, for there is no authority except from God, and those who exist are ordained by God.

3104.text: Therefore he who resists the authority, withstands the ordinance of God; and those who withstand will receive to themselves judgment.

3105.text: For rulers are not a terror to the good work, but to the evil. Do you desire to have no fear of the authority? Do that which is good, and you will have praise from the same,

3106.text: for he is a servant of God to you for good. But if you do that which is evil, be afraid, for he does not bear the sword in vain; for he is a servant of God, an avenger for wrath to him who does evil.

3107.text: Therefore you need to be in subjection, not only because of the wrath, but also for conscience' sake.

3108.text: For this reason you also pay taxes, for they are servants of God's service, attending continually on this very thing.

3109.text: Give therefore to everyone what you owe: taxes to whom taxes are due; customs to whom customs; respect to whom respect; honor to whom honor.

3110.text: Owe no one anything, except to love one another; for he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.

3111.text: For the commandments, "You shall not commit adultery," "You shall not murder," "You shall not steal," "You shall not covet," and whatever other commandments there are, are all summed up in this saying, namely, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."

3112.text: Love does not harm a neighbor. Love therefore is the fulfillment of the law.

3113.text: Do this, knowing the time, that it is already time for you to awaken out of sleep, for salvation is now nearer to us than when we first believed.

3114.text: The night is far gone, and the day is near. Let us therefore throw off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armor of light.

3115.text: Let us walk properly, as in the day; not in reveling and drunkenness, not in sexual promiscuity and lustful acts, and not in strife and jealousy.

3116.text: But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh, for its lusts.

3117.text: Now accept one who is weak in faith, but not for disputes over opinions.

3118.text: One man has faith to eat all things, but he who is weak eats only vegetables.

3119.text: Do not let him who eats despise him who does not eat. Do not let him who does not eat judge him who eats, for God has accepted him.

3120.text: Who are you who judge another's servant? To his own lord he stands or falls. Yes, he will be made to stand, for the Lord has power to make him stand.

3121.text: One man esteems one day as more important. Another esteems every day alike. Let each man be fully assured in his own mind.

3122.text: He who observes the day, observes it to the Lord. He who eats, eats to the Lord, for he gives God thanks. He who does not eat, to the Lord he does not eat, and gives God thanks.

3123.text: For none of us lives to himself, and none dies to himself.
