3124.text: For if we live, we live to the Lord. Or if we die, we die to the Lord. If therefore we live or die, we are the Lord's.

3125.text: For to this end Christ died, and lived again, that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living.

3126.text: But you, why do you judge your brother? Or you again, why do you despise your brother? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of God.

3127.text: For it is written, "'As I live,' says the Lord, 'to me every knee will bow. Every tongue will confess to God.'"

3128.text: So then each one of us will give account of himself to God.

3129.text: Therefore let us not judge one another any more, but judge this rather, that no man put a stumbling block in his brother's way, or an occasion for falling.

3130.text: I know, and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus, that nothing is unclean of itself; except that to him who considers anything to be unclean, to him it is unclean.

3131.text: Yet if because of food your brother is grieved, you walk no longer in love. Do not destroy with your food him for whom Christ died.

3132.text: Then do not let your good be slandered,

3133.text: for the Kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

3134.text: For he who serves Christ in these things is acceptable to God and approved by men.

3135.text: So then, let us follow after things which make for peace, and things by which we may build one another up.

3136.text: Do not overthrow God's work for food's sake. All things indeed are clean, however it is evil for that man who creates a stumbling block by eating.

3137.text: It is good to not eat meat, drink wine, nor do anything by which your brother stumbles.

3138.text: Do you have faith? Have it to yourself before God. Happy is he who does not judge himself in that which he approves.

3139.text: But he who doubts is condemned if he eats, because it is not of faith; and whatever is not of faith is sin.

3140.text: Now we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves.

3141.text: Let each one of us please his neighbor for that which is good, to be building him up.

3142.text: For even Christ did not please himself. But, as it is written, "The reproaches of those who reproached you fell on me."

3143.text: For whatever things were written before were written for our learning, that through patience and through encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.

3144.text: Now the God of patience and of encouragement grant you to be of the same mind one with another according to Christ Jesus,

3145.text: that with one accord you may with one mouth glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

3146.text: Therefore accept one another, even as Christ also accepted you, to the glory of God.

3147.text: Now I say that Christ has been made a servant of the circumcision for the truth of God, that he might confirm the promises given to the fathers,

3148.text: and that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy. As it is written, "Therefore will I give praise to you among the Gentiles, and sing to your name."

3149.text: Again he says, "Rejoice, you Gentiles, with his people."

3150.text: Again, "Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles! Let all the peoples praise him."

3151.text: Again, Isaiah says, "There will be the root of Jesse, he who arises to rule over the Gentiles; in him the Gentiles will hope."

3152.text: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope, in the power of the Holy Spirit.

3153.text: I myself am also persuaded about you, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish others.

3154.text: But I write the more boldly to you in part, as reminding you, because of the grace that was given to me by God,

3155.text: that I should be a servant of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, serving as a priest the Good News of God, that the offering up of the Gentiles might be made acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

3156.text: I have therefore my boasting in Christ Jesus in things pertaining to God.

3157.text: For I will not dare to speak of any things except those which Christ worked through me, for the obedience of the Gentiles, by word and deed,

3158.text: in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Spirit of God; so that from Jerusalem, and around as far as to Illyricum, I have fully preached the Good News of Christ;

3159.text: yes, making it my aim to proclaim the Good News, not where Christ was already named, that I might not build on another's foundation.

3160.text: But, as it is written, "They will see, to whom no news of him came. They who have not heard will understand."

3161.text: Therefore also I was hindered these many times from coming to you,

3162.text: but now, no longer having any place in these regions, and having these many years a longing to come to you,

3163.text: whenever I journey to Spain. For I hope to see you on my journey, and to be helped on my way there by you, if first I may enjoy your company for a while.

3164.text: But now, I say, I am going to Jerusalem, serving the saints.

3165.text: For it has been the good pleasure of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor among the saints who are at Jerusalem.

3166.text: Yes, it has been their good pleasure, and they are their debtors. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, they owe it to them also to serve them in fleshly things.

3167.text: When therefore I have accomplished this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will go on by way of you to Spain.

3168.text: I know that, when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of the Christ.

3169.text: Now I beg you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ, and by the love of the Spirit, that you strive together with me in your prayers to God for me,

3170.text: that I may be delivered from those who are disobedient in Judea, and that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints;

3171.text: that I may come to you in joy through the will of God, and together with you, find rest.

3172.text: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

3173.text: I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, who is a servant of the church that is at Cenchreae,

3174.text: that you receive her in the Lord, in a way worthy of the saints, and that you assist her in whatever matter she may need from you, for she herself also has been a helper of many, and of my own self.

3175.text: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,

3176.text: who for my life, laid down their own necks; to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles.

3177.text: Greet the church that is in their house. Greet Epaenetus, my beloved, who is the first fruits of Asia to Christ.

3178.text: Greet Mary, who labored much for you.

3179.text: Greet Andronicus and Junias, my relatives and my fellow prisoners, who are notable among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.

3180.text: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.

3181.text: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and Stachys, my beloved.

3182.text: Greet Apelles, the approved in Christ. Greet those who are of the household of Aristobulus.

3183.text: Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet them of the household of Narcissus, who are in the Lord.

3184.text: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet Persis, the beloved, who labored much in the Lord.

3185.text: Greet Rufus, the chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

3186.text: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers who are with them.

3187.text: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints who are with them.

3188.text: Greet one another with a holy kiss. The churches of Christ greet you.

3189.text: Now I beg you, brothers, look out for those who are causing the divisions and occasions of stumbling, contrary to the doctrine which you learned, and turn away from them.

3190.text: For those who are such do not serve our Lord, Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by their smooth and flattering speech, they deceive the hearts of the innocent.

3191.text: For your obedience has become known to all. I rejoice therefore over you. But I desire to have you wise in that which is good, but innocent in that which is evil.

3192.text: And the God of peace will quickly crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

3193.text: Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives.

3194.text: I, Tertius, who write the letter, greet you in the Lord.

3195.text: Gaius, my host and host of the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, greets you, as does Quartus, the brother.

3196.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all! Amen.

3197.text: Now to him who is able to establish you according to my Good News and the proclaiming of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery which has been kept secret through long ages,

3198.text: but now is revealed, and by the Scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the eternal God, is made known for obedience of faith to all the nations;

3199.text: to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever! Amen.

3200.text: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,

3201.text: to the church of God which is at Corinth; those who are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, both theirs and ours:

3202.text: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

3203.text: I always thank my God concerning you, for the grace of God which was given you in Christ Jesus;

3204.text: that in everything you were enriched in him, in all speech and all knowledge;

3205.text: even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you:

3206.text: so that you come behind in no gift; waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ;

3207.text: who will also confirm you until the end, blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

3208.text: God is faithful, through whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ, our Lord.

3209.text: Now I beg you, brothers, through the name of our Lord, Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfected together in the same mind and in the same judgment.

3210.text: For it has been reported to me concerning you, my brothers, by those who are from Chloe's household, that there are contentions among you.

3211.text: Now I mean this, that each one of you says, "I follow Paul," "I follow Apollos," "I follow Cephas," and, "I follow Christ."

3212.text: Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized into the name of Paul?

3213.text: I thank God that I baptized none of you, except Crispus and Gaius,

3214.text: so that no one should say that you had been baptized into my own name.

3215.text: (I also baptized the household of Stephanas; besides them, I do not know whether I baptized any other.)

3216.text: For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to proclaim the Good News-not in wisdom of words, so that the cross of Christ would not be made void.

3217.text: For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are dying, but to us who are saved it is the power of God.

3218.text: For it is written, "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, I will bring the discernment of the discerning to nothing."

3219.text: Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the Law scholar of this world? Hasn't God made foolish the wisdom of this world?

3220.text: For seeing that in the wisdom of God, the world through its wisdom did not know God, it was God's good pleasure through the foolishness of the proclaiming to save those who believe.

3221.text: For Jews ask for signs, Greeks seek after wisdom,

3222.text: but we proclaim Christ crucified; a stumbling block to Jews, and foolishness to Gentiles,

3223.text: but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.

3224.text: Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.

3225.text: For you see your calling, brothers, that not many are wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, and not many noble;

3226.text: but God chose the foolish things of the world that he might put to shame those who are wise. God chose the weak things of the world, that he might put to shame the things that are strong;

3227.text: and God chose the lowly things of the world, and the things that are despised, and the things that are not, that he might bring to nothing the things that are:

3228.text: that no flesh should boast before God.

3229.text: But of him, you are in Christ Jesus, who was made to us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification, and redemption:

3230.text: that, according as it is written, "He who boasts, let him boast in the Lord."

3231.text: When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with excellence of speech or of wisdom, proclaiming to you the mystery of God.

3232.text: For I determined not to know anything among you, except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.

3233.text: I was with you in weakness, in fear, and in much trembling.

3234.text: My speech and my proclaiming were not in persuasive words of wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power,

3235.text: that your faith would not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.

3236.text: We speak wisdom, however, among those who are full grown; yet a wisdom not of this world, nor of the rulers of this world, who are coming to nothing.

3237.text: But we speak God's wisdom in a mystery, the wisdom that has been hidden, which God foreordained before the worlds for our glory,

3238.text: which none of the rulers of this world has known. For had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

3239.text: But as it is written, "Things which an eye did not see, and an ear did not hear, which did not enter into the heart of man, these God has prepared for those who love him."

3240.text: But to us, God revealed them through the Spirit. For the Spirit searches all things, yes, the deep things of God.

3241.text: For who among men knows the things of a man, except the spirit of the man, which is in him? Even so, no one knows the things of God, except God's Spirit.

3242.text: But we received, not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit which is from God, that we might know the things that were freely given to us by God.

3243.text: Which things also we speak, not in words which man's wisdom teaches, but which the Spirit teaches, comparing spiritual things with spiritual things.

3244.text: Now the natural man does not receive the things of God's Spirit, for they are foolishness to him, and he cannot know them, because they are spiritually discerned.

3245.text: But he who is spiritual discerns all things, and he himself is judged by no one.

3246.text: "For who has known the mind of the Lord, that he should instruct him?" But we have Christ's mind.

3247.text: Brothers, I could not speak to you as to spiritual, but as to fleshly, as to babies in Christ.

3248.text: I fed you with milk, not with meat; for you weren't yet ready. Indeed, not even now are you ready,

3249.text: for you are still fleshly. For insofar as there is jealousy, strife, and factions among you, are not you fleshly, and do you not walk in the ways of men?

3250.text: For when one says, "I follow Paul," and another, "I follow Apollos," are not you men?

3251.text: Who then is Apollos, and who is Paul, but servants through whom you believed; and each as the Lord gave to him?

3252.text: I planted. Apollos watered. But God gave the increase.

3253.text: So then neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase.

3254.text: Now he who plants and he who waters are the same, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.

3255.text: For we are God's fellow workers. You are God's farming, God's building.

3256.text: According to the grace of God which was given to me, as a wise master builder I laid a foundation, and another builds on it. But let each man be careful how he builds on it.

3257.text: For no one can lay any other foundation than that which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ.

3258.text: But if anyone builds on the foundation with gold, silver, costly stones, wood, hay, or stubble;

3259.text: each man's work will be revealed. For the Day will declare it, because it is revealed in fire; and the fire itself will test what sort of work each man's work is.

3260.text: If any man's work remains which he built on it, he will receive a reward.

3261.text: If any man's work is burned, he will suffer loss, but he himself will be saved, but as through fire.

3262.text: Do you not know that you are a temple of God, and that God's Spirit lives in you?

3263.text: If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him; for God's temple is holy, which you are.

3264.text: Let no one deceive himself. If anyone thinks that he is wise among you in this world, let him become a fool, that he may become wise.

3265.text: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, "He has taken the wise in their craftiness."

3266.text: And again, "The Lord knows the reasoning of the wise, that it is worthless."

3267.text: Therefore let no one boast in men. For all things are yours,

3268.text: whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come. All are yours,

3269.text: and you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.

3270.text: So let a man think of us as Christ's servants, and stewards of God's mysteries.

3271.text: Here, moreover, it is required of stewards, that they be found faithful.

3272.text: But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged by you, or by man's judgment. Yes, I do not judge my own self.

3273.text: For I know nothing against myself. Yet I am not justified by this, but he who judges me is the Lord.

3274.text: Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and reveal the counsels of the hearts. Then each man will get his praise from God.

3275.text: Now these things, brothers, I have in a figure transferred to myself and Apollos for your sakes, that in us you might learn not to go beyond the things which are written, that none of you be puffed up against one another.

3276.text: For who makes you different? And what do you have that you did not receive? But if you did receive it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?

3277.text: You are already filled. You have already become rich. You have come to reign without us. Yes, and I wish that you did reign, that we also might reign with you.

3278.text: For, I think that God has displayed us, the apostles, last of all, like men sentenced to death. For we are made a spectacle to the world, both to angels and men.

3279.text: We are fools for Christ's sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You have honor, but we have dishonor.

3280.text: Even to this present hour we hunger, thirst, are naked, are beaten, and have no certain dwelling place.

3281.text: We toil, working with our own hands. When people curse us, we bless. Being persecuted, we endure.

3282.text: Being defamed, we entreat. We are made as the filth of the world, the dirt wiped off by all, even until now.

3283.text: I do not write these things to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved children.

3284.text: For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, yet not many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News.

3285.text: I beg you therefore, be imitators of me.

3286.text: Because of this I have sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways which are in Christ, even as I teach everywhere in every church.

3287.text: Now some are puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.

3288.text: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing. And I will know, not the word of those who are puffed up, but the power.

3289.text: For the Kingdom of God is not in word, but in power.

3290.text: What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?

3291.text: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and such sexual immorality as is not even among the Gentiles, that one has his father's wife.

3292.text: You are puffed up, and did not rather mourn, that he who had done this deed might be removed from among you.

3293.text: For I most certainly, as being absent in body but present in spirit, have already, as though I were present, judged him who has done this thing.

3294.text: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, you being gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,

3295.text: are to deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.

3296.text: Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little yeast leavens the whole lump?

3297.text: Purge out the old yeast, that you may be a new lump, even as you are unleavened. For indeed Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed.

3298.text: Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old yeast, neither with the yeast of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

3299.text: I wrote to you in my letter to have no company with sexual sinners;

3300.text: yet not at all meaning with the sexual sinners of this world, or with the covetous and extortioners, or with idolaters; for then you would have to leave the world.

3301.text: But as it is, I wrote to you not to associate with anyone who is called a brother who is a sexual sinner, or covetous, or an idolater, or a slanderer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner. Do not even eat with such a person.

3302.text: For what have I to do with also judging those who are outside? Do you not judge those who are within?

3303.text: But those who are outside, God judges. "Put away the wicked man from among yourselves."

3304.text: Dare any of you, having a matter against his neighbor, go to law before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?

3305.text: Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?

3306.text: Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more, things that pertain to this life?

3307.text: If then, you have to judge things pertaining to this life, do you set them to judge who are of no account in the church?

3308.text: I say this to move you to shame. Is not there even one wise man among you who would be able to decide between his brothers?

3309.text: But brother goes to law with brother, and that before unbelievers!

3310.text: Therefore it is already altogether a defect in you, that you have lawsuits one with another. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?

3311.text: No, but you yourselves do wrong, and defraud, and that against your brothers.

3312.text: Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the Kingdom of God? Do not be deceived. Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor male prostitutes, nor men who practice sexual relations with men,

3313.text: nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor slanderers, nor extortioners, will inherit the Kingdom of God.

3314.text: Such were some of you, but you were washed. But you were sanctified. But you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and in the Spirit of our God.

3315.text: "All things are lawful for me," but not all things are expedient. "All things are lawful for me," but I will not be brought under the power of anything.

3316.text: "Foods for the belly, and the belly for foods," but God will bring to nothing both it and them. But the body is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body.

3317.text: Now God raised up the Lord, and will also raise us up by his power.

3318.text: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them members of a prostitute? May it never be!

3319.text: Or do you not know that he who is joined to a prostitute is one body? For, "The two," says he, "will become one flesh."

3320.text: But he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit.

3321.text: Flee sexual immorality! "Every sin that a man does is outside the body," but he who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.

3322.text: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit which is in you, which you have from God? You are not your own,

3323.text: for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body.

3324.text: Now concerning the things about which you wrote: it is good for a man not to touch a woman.

3325.text: But, because of sexual immoralities, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.

3326.text: Let the husband fulfill his marital duty to his wife, and likewise also the wife to her husband.

3327.text: The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband. Likewise also the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife.

3328.text: Do not deprive one another, unless it is by consent for a season, that you may give yourselves to prayer, and may be together again, that Satan does not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.

3329.text: But this I say by way of concession, not of commandment.

3330.text: Yet I wish that all men were like me. However each man has his own gift from God, one of this kind, and another of that kind.

3331.text: But I say to the unmarried and to widows, it is good for them if they remain even as I am.

3332.text: But if they do not have self-control, let them marry. For it's better to marry than to burn.

3333.text: But to the married I command-not I, but the Lord-that the wife not leave her husband

3334.text: (but if she departs, let her remain unmarried, or else be reconciled to her husband), and that the husband not leave his wife.

3335.text: But to the rest I-not the Lord-say, if any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she is content to live with him, let him not leave her.

3336.text: The woman who has an unbelieving husband, and he is content to live with her, let her not leave her husband.

3337.text: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the brother. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.

3338.text: Yet if the unbeliever departs, let there be separation. The brother or the sister is not under bondage in such cases, but God has called us to peace.

3339.text: For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?

3340.text: Only, as the Lord has distributed to each man, as God has called each, so let him walk. So I command in all the churches.

3341.text: Was anyone called having been circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.

3342.text: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God.

3343.text: Let each man stay in that calling in which he was called.

3344.text: Were you called being a bondservant? Do not let that bother you, but if you get an opportunity to become free, use it.

3345.text: For he who was called in the Lord being a bondservant is the Lord's free man. Likewise he who was called being free is Christ's bondservant.

3346.text: You were bought with a price. Do not become bondservants of men.

3347.text: Brothers, let each man, in whatever condition he was called, stay in that condition with God.

3348.text: Now concerning virgins, I have no commandment from the Lord, but I give my judgment as one who has obtained mercy from the Lord to be trustworthy.

3349.text: I think that it is good therefore, because of the distress that is on us, that it is good for a man to be as he is.

3350.text: Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be freed. Are you free from a wife? Do not seek a wife.

3351.text: But if you marry, you have not sinned. If a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such will have oppression in the flesh, and I want to spare you.

3352.text: But I say this, brothers: the time is short, that from now on, both those who have wives may be as though they had none;

3353.text: and those who weep, as though they did not weep; and those who rejoice, as though they did not rejoice; and those who buy, as though they did not possess;

3354.text: and those who use the world, as not using it to the fullest. For the mode of this world passes away.

3355.text: But I desire to have you to be free from cares. He who is unmarried is concerned for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord;

3356.text: but he who is married is concerned about the things of the world, how he may please his wife.

3357.text: There is also a difference between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman cares about the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But she who is married cares about the things of the world-how she may please her husband.

3358.text: This I say for your own profit; not that I may ensnare you, but for that which is appropriate, and that you may attend to the Lord without distraction.

3359.text: But if any man thinks that he is behaving inappropriately toward his virgin, if she is past the flower of her age, and if need so requires, let him do what he desires. He does not sin. Let them marry.

3360.text: But he who stands steadfast in his heart, having no necessity, but has power over his own heart, to keep his own virgin, does well.

3361.text: So then both he who gives his own virgin in marriage does well, and he who does not give her in marriage does better.

3362.text: A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives; but if the husband is dead, she is free to be married to whomever she desires, only in the Lord.

3363.text: But she is happier if she stays as she is, in my judgment, and I think that I also have God's Spirit.

3364.text: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

3365.text: But if anyone thinks that he knows anything, he does not yet know as he ought to know.

3366.text: But if anyone loves God, the same is known by him.

3367.text: Therefore concerning the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that no idol is anything in the world, and that there is no God but one.

3368.text: For though there are things that are called "gods," whether in the heavens or on earth; as there are many "gods" and many "lords;"

3369.text: yet to us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things, and we for him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we live through him.

3370.text: However, that knowledge is not in all men. But some, being so accustomed to idols until now, eat as of a thing sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.

3371.text: But food will not commend us to God. For neither, if we do not eat, are we the worse; nor, if we eat, are we the better.

3372.text: But be careful that by no means does this liberty of yours become a stumbling block to the weak.

3373.text: For if a man sees you who have knowledge sitting in an idol's temple, won't his conscience, if he is weak, be emboldened to eat things sacrificed to idols?

3374.text: And through your knowledge, he who is weak perishes, the brother for whom the Christ died.

3375.text: Thus, sinning against the brothers, and wounding their conscience when it is weak, you sin against Christ.

3376.text: Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will eat no meat forevermore, that I do not cause my brother to stumble.

3377.text: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have not I seen Jesus Christ, our Lord? Are not you my work in the Lord?

3378.text: If to others I am not an apostle, yet at least I am to you; for you are the seal of my office of apostle in the Lord.

3379.text: My defense to those who examine me is this.

3380.text: Have we no right to eat and to drink?

3381.text: Have we no right to take along a wife who is a believer, even as the rest of the apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?

3382.text: Or have only Barnabas and I no right to not work?

3383.text: What soldier ever serves at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard, and does not eat of its fruit? Or who feeds a flock, and does not drink from the flock's milk?

3384.text: Do I speak these things according to the ways of men? Or does not the Law also say the same thing?

3385.text: For it is written in the Law of Moses, "You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain." Is it for the oxen that God cares,

3386.text: or does he say it assuredly for our sake? Yes, it was written for our sake, because he who plows ought to plow in hope, and he who threshes in the hope of having a share.

3387.text: If we sowed to you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we reap your fleshly things?

3388.text: If others partake of this right over you, do not we yet more? Nevertheless we did not use this right, but we bear all things, that we may cause no hindrance to the Good News of Christ.

3389.text: Do you not know that those who serve around sacred things eat from the things of the temple, and those who wait on the altar have their portion with the altar?

3390.text: Even so the Lord ordained that those who proclaim the Good News should live from the Good News.

3391.text: But I have used none of these things, and I do not write these things that it may be done so in my case; for I would rather die, than that anyone should make my boasting void.

3392.text: For if I proclaim the Good News, I have nothing to boast about; for necessity is laid on me; but woe is to me, if I do not proclaim the Good News.

3393.text: For if I do this of my own will, I have a reward. But if not of my own will, I have a stewardship entrusted to me.

3394.text: What then is my reward? That, when I proclaim the Good News, I may present the Good News without charge, so as not to abuse my authority in the Good News.

3395.text: For though I was free from all, I brought myself under bondage to all, that I might gain the more.

3396.text: To the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain Jews; to those who are under the law, as under the law, not being myself under the law, that I might gain those who are under the law;

3397.text: to those who are without law, as without law (not being without law toward God, but under law toward Christ), that I might win those who are without law.

3398.text: To the weak I became as weak, that I might gain the weak. I have become all things to all men, that I may by all means save some.

3399.text: Now I do all things for the sake of the Good News, that I may be a joint partaker of it.

3400.text: Do you not know that those who run in a race all run, but one receives the prize? Run like that, that you may win.

3401.text: Every man who strives in the games exercises self-control in all things. Now they do it to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible.

3402.text: I therefore run like that, as not uncertainly. I fight like that, as not beating the air,

3403.text: but I beat my body and bring it into submission, lest by any means, after I have preached to others, I myself should be rejected.

3404.text: Now I would not have you ignorant, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;

3405.text: and were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea;

3406.text: and all ate the same spiritual food;

3407.text: and all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank of a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.

3408.text: However with most of them, God was not well pleased, for they were overthrown in the wilderness.

3409.text: Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.

3410.text: Neither be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written, "The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play."

3411.text: Neither let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them committed, and in one day twenty-three thousand fell.

3412.text: Neither let us test the Lord, as some of them tested, and perished by the serpents.

3413.text: Neither grumble, as some of them also grumbled, and perished by the destroyer.

3414.text: Now all these things happened to them by way of example, and they were written for our admonition, on whom the ends of the ages have come.

3415.text: Therefore let him who thinks he stands be careful that he does not fall.

3416.text: No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.

3417.text: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

3418.text: I speak as to wise men. Judge what I say.

3419.text: The cup of blessing which we bless, is not it a sharing of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is not it a sharing of the body of Christ?

3420.text: Because there is one loaf of bread, we, who are many, are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf of bread.

3421.text: Consider Israel according to the flesh. Do not those who eat the sacrifices participate in the altar?

3422.text: What am I saying then? That a thing sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything?

3423.text: But I say that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons, and not to God, and I do not desire that you would have fellowship with demons.

3424.text: You cannot both drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot both partake of the table of the Lord, and of the table of demons.

3425.text: Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?

3426.text: "All things are lawful," but not all things are profitable. "All things are lawful," but not all things build up.

3427.text: Let no one seek his own, but his neighbor's good.

3428.text: Whatever is sold in the butcher shop, eat, asking no question for the sake of conscience,

3429.text: for "the earth is the Lord's, and its fullness."

3430.text: But if one of those who do not believe invites you to a meal, and you are inclined to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for the sake of conscience.

3431.text: But if anyone says to you, "This was offered to idols," do not eat it for the sake of the one who told you, and for the sake of conscience.

3432.text: Conscience, I say, not your own, but the other's conscience. For why is my liberty judged by another conscience?

3433.text: If I partake with thankfulness, why am I denounced for that for which I give thanks?

3434.text: Whether therefore you eat, or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.

3435.text: Give no occasions for stumbling, either to Jews, or to Greeks, or to the church of God;

3436.text: even as I also please all men in all things, not seeking my own profit, but the profit of the many, that they may be saved.

3437.text: Be imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ.

3438.text: Now I praise you, that you remember me in all things, and hold firm the traditions, even as I delivered them to you.

3439.text: But I would have you know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.

3440.text: Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonors his head.

3441.text: But every woman praying or prophesying with her head unveiled dishonors her head. For it is one and the same thing as if she were shaved.

3442.text: For if a woman is not covered, let her also be shorn. But if it is shameful for a woman to be shorn or shaved, let her be covered.

3443.text: For a man indeed ought not to have his head covered, because he is the image and glory of God, but the woman is the glory of the man.

3444.text: For man is not from woman, but woman from man;

3445.text: for neither was man created for the woman, but woman for the man.

3446.text: For this cause the woman ought to have authority on her head, because of the angels.

3447.text: Nevertheless, neither is the woman independent of the man, nor the man independent of the woman, in the Lord.

3448.text: For as woman came from man, so a man also comes through a woman; but all things are from God.

3449.text: Judge for yourselves. Is it appropriate that a woman pray to God unveiled?

3450.text: Doesn't even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a dishonor to him?

3451.text: But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her, for her hair is given to her for a covering.

3452.text: But if any man seems to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither do God's churches.

3453.text: But in giving you this command, I do not praise you, that you come together not for the better but for the worse.

3454.text: For first of all, when you come together in the church, I hear that divisions exist among you, and I partly believe it.

3455.text: For there also must be factions among you, that those who are approved may be revealed among you.

3456.text: When therefore you assemble yourselves together, it is not the Lord's supper that you eat.

3457.text: For in your eating each one takes his own supper first. One is hungry, and another is drunken.

3458.text: What, do you not have houses to eat and to drink in? Or do you despise God's church, and put them to shame who do not have? What shall I tell you? Shall I praise you? In this I do not praise you.

3459.text: For I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was betrayed took bread.

3460.text: When he had given thanks, he broke it, and said, "This is my body, which is for you. Do this in memory of me."

3461.text: In the same way he also took the cup, after supper, saying, "This cup is the New Covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in memory of me."

3462.text: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.

3463.text: Therefore whoever eats this bread or drinks the Lord's cup in a manner unworthy will be guilty of the body and the blood of the Lord.

3464.text: But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of the bread, and drink of the cup.

3465.text: For he who eats and drinks eats and drinks judgment to himself, if he does not discern the body.

3466.text: For this cause many among you are weak and sickly, and not a few sleep.

3467.text: For if we discerned ourselves, we would not be judged.

3468.text: But when we are judged, we are punished by the Lord, that we may not be condemned with the world.

3469.text: Therefore, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait one for another.

3470.text: But if anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, lest your coming together be for judgment. The rest I will set in order whenever I come.

3471.text: Now concerning spiritual things, brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant.

3472.text: You know that when you were heathen, you were led away to those mute idols, however you might be led.

3473.text: Therefore I make known to you that no man speaking by God's Spirit says, "Jesus is accursed." No one can say, "Jesus is Lord," but by the Holy Spirit.

3474.text: Now there are various kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.

3475.text: There are various kinds of service, and the same Lord.

3476.text: There are various kinds of workings, but the same God, who works all things in all.

3477.text: But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.

3478.text: For to one is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom, and to another the word of knowledge, according to the same Spirit;

3479.text: to another faith, by the same Spirit; and to another gifts of healings, by the one Spirit;

3480.text: and to another workings of miracles; and to another prophecy; and to another discerning of spirits; to another different kinds of languages; and to another the interpretation of languages.

3481.text: But the one and the same Spirit works all of these, distributing to each one separately as he desires.

3482.text: For as the body is one, and has many members, and all the members of the body, being many, are one body; so also is Christ.

3483.text: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether bond or free; and were all given to drink of one Spirit.

3484.text: For the body is not one member, but many.

3485.text: If the foot would say, "Because I'm not the hand, I'm not part of the body," it is not therefore not part of the body.

3486.text: If the ear would say, "Because I'm not the eye, I'm not part of the body," it's not therefore not part of the body.

3487.text: If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the smelling be?

3488.text: But now God has set the members, each one of them, in the body, just as he desired.

3489.text: If they were all one member, where would the body be?

3490.text: But now they are many members, but one body.

3491.text: The eye cannot tell the hand, "I have no need for you," or again the head to the feet, "I have no need for you."

3492.text: No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.

3493.text: Those parts of the body which we think to be less honorable, on those we bestow more abundant honor; and our unpresentable parts have more abundant propriety;

3494.text: whereas our presentable parts have no such need. But God composed the body together, giving more abundant honor to the inferior part,

3495.text: that there should be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for one another.

3496.text: When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. Or when one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.

3497.text: Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.

3498.text: God has set some in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracle workers, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, and various kinds of languages.

3499.text: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all miracle workers?

3500.text: Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with various languages? Do all interpret?

3501.text: But earnestly desire the greater gifts. Moreover, I show a most excellent way to you.

3502.text: If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but do not have love, I have become sounding brass, or a clanging cymbal.

3503.text: If I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge; and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.

3504.text: If I dole out all my goods to feed the poor, and if I surrender my body so that I may boast, but do not have love, it profits me nothing.

3505.text: Love is patient and is kind; love does not envy. Love does not brag, is not proud,

3506.text: doesn't behave itself inappropriately, does not seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil;

3507.text: doesn't rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth;

3508.text: bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

3509.text: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will be done away with. Where there are various languages, they will cease. Where there is knowledge, it will be done away with.

3510.text: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part;

3511.text: but when that which is complete has come, then that which is partial will be done away with.

3512.text: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I felt as a child, I thought as a child. Now that I have become a man, I have put away childish things.

3513.text: For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know fully, even as I was also fully known.

3514.text: But now faith, hope, and love remain-these three. The greatest of these is love.

3515.text: Follow after love, and earnestly desire spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy.

3516.text: For he who speaks in another language speaks not to men, but to God; for no one understands; but in the Spirit he speaks mysteries.

3517.text: But he who prophesies speaks to men for their encouragement, strengthening, and comfort.

3518.text: He who speaks in another language edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the church.

3519.text: Now I desire to have you all speak with other languages, but rather that you would prophesy, and he is greater who prophesies than he who speaks with other languages, unless he interprets, that the church may be built up.

3520.text: But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking with other languages, what would I profit you, unless I speak to you either by way of revelation, or of knowledge, or of prophesying, or of teaching?

3521.text: Even things without life, giving a voice, whether pipe or harp, if they did not give a distinction in the sounds, how would it be known what is piped or harped?

3522.text: For if the trumpet gave an uncertain sound, who would prepare himself for war?

3523.text: So also you, unless you uttered by the tongue words easy to understand, how would it be known what is spoken? For you would be speaking into the air.

3524.text: There are, it may be, so many kinds of sounds in the world, and none is without meaning.

3525.text: If then I do not know the meaning of the sound, I would be to him who speaks a foreigner, and he who speaks would be a foreigner to me.

3526.text: So also you, since you are zealous for spiritual gifts, seek that you may abound to the building up of the church.

3527.text: Therefore let him who speaks in another language pray that he may interpret.

3528.text: For if I pray in another language, my spirit prays, but my understanding is unfruitful.

3529.text: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also. I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.

3530.text: Otherwise if you bless with the spirit, how will he who fills the place of the unlearned say the "Amen" at your giving of thanks, seeing he does not know what you say?

3531.text: For you truly give thanks well, but the other person is not built up.

3532.text: I thank God, I speak with other languages more than you all.

3533.text: However in the church I would rather speak five words with my understanding, that I might instruct others also, than ten thousand words in another language.

3534.text: Brothers, do not be children in thoughts, yet in malice be babies, but in thoughts be mature.

3535.text: In the law it is written, "By men of strange languages and by the lips of strangers I will speak to this people. Not even thus will they hear me, says the Lord."

3536.text: Therefore other languages are for a sign, not to those who believe, but to the unbelieving; but prophesying is for a sign, not to the unbelieving, but to those who believe.

3537.text: If therefore the whole church is assembled together and all speak with other languages, and unlearned or unbelieving people come in, won't they say that you are crazy?

3538.text: But if all prophesy, and someone unbelieving or unlearned comes in, he is reproved by all, and he is judged by all.

3539.text: And thus the secrets of his heart are revealed. So he will fall down on his face and worship God, declaring that God is among you indeed.

3540.text: What is it then, brothers? When you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has another language, has an interpretation. Let all things be done to build each other up.

3541.text: If any man speaks in another language, let it be two, or at the most three, and in turn; and let one interpret.

3542.text: But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the church, and let him speak to himself, and to God.

3543.text: Let the prophets speak, two or three, and let the others discern.

3544.text: But if a revelation is made to another sitting by, let the first keep silent.

3545.text: For you can all prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all may be encouraged.

3546.text: The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets,

3547.text: for God is not a God of confusion, but of peace. As in all the churches of the saints,

3548.text: let the women keep silent in the churches, for it has not been permitted for them to speak; but let them be in subjection, as the Law also says.

3549.text: If they desire to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a woman to chatter in the church.

3550.text: What? Was it from you that the word of God went out? Or did it come to you alone?

3551.text: If any man thinks himself to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him recognize the things which I write to you, that they are the commandment of the Lord.

3552.text: But if someone does not recognize this, he is not recognized.

3553.text: Therefore, brothers, desire earnestly to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking with other languages.

3554.text: Let all things be done decently and in order.

3555.text: Now I declare to you, brothers, the Good News which I preached to you, which also you received, in which you also stand,

3556.text: by which also you are saved, if you hold firmly the word which I preached to you-unless you believed in vain.

3557.text: For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,

3558.text: that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,

3559.text: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.

3560.text: Then he appeared to over five hundred brothers at once, most of whom remain until now, but some have also fallen asleep.

3561.text: Then he appeared to Jacob, then to all the apostles,

3562.text: and last of all, as to the child born at the wrong time, he appeared to me also.

3563.text: For I am the least of the apostles, who is not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

3564.text: But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was bestowed on me was not futile, but I worked more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.

3565.text: Whether then it is I or they, so we proclaim, and so you believed.

3566.text: Now if Christ is preached, that he has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?

3567.text: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised.

3568.text: If Christ has not been raised, then our proclaiming is in vain, and your faith also is in vain.

3569.text: Yes, we are found false witnesses of God, because we testified about God that he raised up Christ, whom he did not raise up, if it is so that the dead are not raised.

3570.text: For if the dead are not raised, neither has Christ been raised.

3571.text: If Christ has not been raised, your faith is vain; you are still in your sins.

3572.text: Then they also who are fallen asleep in Christ have perished.

3573.text: If we have only hoped in Christ in this life, we are of all men most pitiable.

3574.text: But now Christ has been raised from the dead, the first fruits of those who are asleep.

3575.text: For since death came by man, the resurrection of the dead also came by man.

3576.text: For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.

3577.text: But each in his own order: Christ the first fruits, then those who are Christ's, at his coming.

3578.text: Then the end comes, when he will deliver up the Kingdom to God, even the Father; when he will have abolished all rule and all authority and power.

3579.text: For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.

3580.text: The last enemy that will be abolished is death.

3581.text: For, "He put all things in subjection under his feet." But when he says, "All things are put in subjection," it is evident that he is excepted who subjected all things to him.

3582.text: When all things have been subjected to him, then the Son will also himself be subjected to him who subjected all things to him, that God may be all in all.

3583.text: Or else what will they do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why then are they baptized for them?

3584.text: Why do we also stand in jeopardy every hour?

3585.text: I affirm, by the boasting in you which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.

3586.text: If I fought with animals at Ephesus for human purposes, what does it profit me? If the dead are not raised, then "let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die."

3587.text: Do not be deceived! "Evil companionships corrupt good morals."

3588.text: Wake up righteously, and do not sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.

3589.text: But someone will say, "How are the dead raised?" and, "With what kind of body do they come?"

3590.text: You foolish one, that which you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies.

3591.text: That which you sow, you do not sow the body that will be, but a bare grain, maybe of wheat, or of some other kind.

3592.text: But God gives it a body even as it pleased him, and to each seed a body of its own.

3593.text: All flesh is not the same flesh, but there is one flesh of men, another flesh of animals, another of fish, and another of birds.

3594.text: There are also celestial bodies, and terrestrial bodies; but the glory of the celestial differs from that of the terrestrial.

3595.text: There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differs from another star in glory.

3596.text: So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption.

3597.text: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.

3598.text: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body and there is also a spiritual body.

3599.text: So also it is written, "The first man, Adam, became a living soul." The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.

3600.text: However that which is spiritual is not first, but that which is natural, then that which is spiritual.

3601.text: The first man is of the earth, made of dust. The second man is from heaven.

3602.text: As is the one made of dust, such are those who are also made of dust; and as is the heavenly, such are they also that are heavenly.

3603.text: As we have borne the image of those made of dust, we will also bear the image of the heavenly.

3604.text: Now I say this, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the Kingdom of God; neither does corruption inherit incorruption.

3605.text: Behold, I tell you a mystery. We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed,

3606.text: in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.

3607.text: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.

3608.text: But when this corruptible will have put on incorruption, and this mortal will have put on immortality, then what is written will happen: "Death is swallowed up in victory."

3609.text: "Death, where is your victory? Death, where is your sting?"

3610.text: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.

3611.text: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

3612.text: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord's work, because you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.

3613.text: Now concerning the collection for the saints, as I commanded the churches of Galatia, you do likewise.

3614.text: On the first day of the week, let each one of you save, as he may prosper, that no collections be made when I come.

3615.text: When I arrive, I will send whoever you approve with letters to carry your gracious gift to Jerusalem.

3616.text: If it is appropriate for me to go also, they will go with me.

3617.text: But I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia.

3618.text: But with you it may be that I will stay, or even winter, that you may send me on my journey wherever I go.

3619.text: For I do not wish to see you now in passing, but I hope to stay a while with you, if the Lord permits.

3620.text: But I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost,

3621.text: for a great and effective door has opened to me, and there are many adversaries.

3622.text: Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear, for he does the work of the Lord, as I also do.

3623.text: Therefore let no one despise him. But set him forward on his journey in peace, that he may come to me; for I expect him with the brothers.

3624.text: Now concerning Apollos, the brother, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers; and it was not at all his desire to come now; but he will come when he has an opportunity.

3625.text: Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong!

3626.text: Let all that you do be done in love.

3627.text: Now I beg you, brothers (you know the house of Stephanas, that it is the first fruits of Achaia, and that they have set themselves to serve the saints),

3628.text: that you also be in subjection to such, and to everyone who helps in the work and labors.

3629.text: I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus; for that which was lacking on your part, they supplied.

3630.text: For they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore acknowledge those who are like that.

3631.text: The churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you much in the Lord, together with the church that is in their house.

3632.text: All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.

3633.text: This greeting is by me, Paul, with my own hand.

3634.text: If any man does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. Come, Lord!

3635.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

3636.text: My love to all of you in Christ Jesus.

3637.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother, to the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints who are in the whole of Achaia:

3638.text: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

3639.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort;

3640.text: who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.

3641.text: For as the sufferings of Christ abound to us, even so our comfort also abounds through Christ.

3642.text: But if we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation. If we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which produces in you the patient enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer.

3643.text: Our hope for you is steadfast, knowing that, since you are partakers of the sufferings, so also are you of the comfort.

3644.text: For we do not desire to have you uninformed, brothers, concerning our affliction which happened in Asia, that we were weighed down exceedingly, beyond our power, so much that we despaired even of life.

3645.text: Yes, we ourselves have had the sentence of death within ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead,

3646.text: who delivered us out of so great a death, and does deliver; on whom we have set our hope that he will also still deliver us;

3647.text: you also helping together on our behalf by your supplication; that, for the gift bestowed on us by means of many, thanks may be given by many persons on our behalf.

3648.text: For our boasting is this: the testimony of our conscience, that in holiness and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God we behaved ourselves in the world, and more abundantly toward you.

3649.text: For we write no other things to you, than what you read or even acknowledge, and I hope you will acknowledge to the end;

3650.text: as also you acknowledged us in part, that we are your boasting, even as you also are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus.

3651.text: In this confidence, I was determined to come first to you, that you might have a second benefit;

3652.text: and by you to pass into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and to be sent forward by you on my journey to Judea.

3653.text: When I therefore was thus determined, did I show fickleness? Or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be the "Yes, yes" and the "No, no?"

3654.text: But as God is faithful, our word toward you is not "Yes and no."

3655.text: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, by me, Silvanus, and Timothy, was not "Yes and no," but in him is "Yes."

3656.text: For however many are the promises of God, in him they are "Yes." Therefore also through him they are "Amen," to the glory of God through us.

3657.text: Now he who establishes us with you in Christ, and anointed us, is God;

3658.text: who also sealed us, and gave us the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts.

3659.text: But I call God for a witness to my soul, that I did not come to Corinth to spare you.

3660.text: Not that we have lordship over your faith, but are fellow workers with you for your joy. For you stand firm in faith.

3661.text: But I determined this for myself, that I would not come to you again in sorrow.

3662.text: For if I make you sorry, then who will make me glad but he who is made sorry by me?

3663.text: And I wrote this very thing, so that, when I came, I would not have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all, that my joy would be shared by all of you.

3664.text: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears, not that you should be made sorry, but that you might know the love that I have so abundantly for you.

3665.text: But if any has caused sorrow, he has caused sorrow, not to me, but in part (that I not press too heavily) to you all.

3666.text: Sufficient to such a one is this punishment which was inflicted by the many;

3667.text: so that on the contrary you should rather forgive him and comfort him, lest by any means such a one should be swallowed up with his excessive sorrow.

3668.text: Therefore I beg you to confirm your love toward him.

3669.text: For to this end I also wrote, that I might know the proof of you, whether you are obedient in all things.

3670.text: Now I also forgive whomever you forgive anything. For if indeed I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven that one for your sakes in the presence of Christ,

3671.text: that no advantage may be gained over us by Satan; for we are not ignorant of his schemes.

3672.text: Now when I came to Troas for the Good News of Christ, and when a door was opened to me in the Lord,

3673.text: I had no relief for my spirit, because I did not find Titus, my brother, but taking my leave of them, I went out into Macedonia.

3674.text: Now thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ, and reveals through us the sweet aroma of his knowledge in every place.

3675.text: For we are a sweet aroma of Christ to God, in those who are saved, and in those who perish;

3676.text: to the one a stench from death to death; to the other a sweet aroma from life to life. Who is sufficient for these things?

3677.text: For we are not as so many, peddling the word of God. But as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God, we speak in Christ.

3678.text: Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? We do not need, as do some, letters of commendation to you or from you, do we?

3679.text: You are our letter, written in our hearts, known and read by all men;

3680.text: being revealed that you are a letter of Christ, served by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tablets of stone, but in tablets that are hearts of flesh.

3681.text: Such confidence we have through Christ toward God;

3682.text: not that we are sufficient of ourselves, to account anything as from ourselves; but our sufficiency is from God;

3683.text: who also made us sufficient as servants of a New Covenant; not of the letter, but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

3684.text: But if the service of death, written engraved on stones, came with glory, so that the children of Israel could not look steadfastly on the face of Moses for the glory of his face; which was passing away:

3685.text: won't service of the Spirit be with much more glory?

3686.text: For if the service of condemnation has glory, the service of righteousness exceeds much more in glory.

3687.text: For truly that which has been made glorious has not been made glorious in this respect, by reason of the glory that surpasses.

3688.text: For if that which passes away was with glory, much more that which remains is in glory.

3689.text: Having therefore such a hope, we use great boldness of speech,

3690.text: and not as Moses, who put a veil on his face, that the children of Israel would not look steadfastly on the end of that which was passing away.

3691.text: But their minds were hardened, for until this very day at the reading of the old covenant the same veil remains, because in Christ it passes away.

3692.text: But to this day, when Moses is read, a veil lies on their heart.

3693.text: But whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

3694.text: Now the Lord is the Spirit and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

3695.text: But we all, with unveiled face beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, the Spirit.

3696.text: Therefore seeing we have this ministry, even as we obtained mercy, we do not faint.

3697.text: But we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God.

3698.text: Even if our Good News is veiled, it is veiled in those who perish;

3699.text: in whom the god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, to prevent the light shining from the Good News of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.

3700.text: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus' sake;

3701.text: seeing it is God who said, "Light will shine out of darkness," who has shone in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

3702.text: But we have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God, and not from ourselves.

3703.text: We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair;

3704.text: pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed;

3705.text: always carrying in the body the putting to death of the Lord Jesus, that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.

3706.text: For we who live are always delivered to death for Jesus' sake, that the life also of Jesus may be revealed in our mortal flesh.

3707.text: So then death works in us, but life in you.

3708.text: But having the same spirit of faith, according to that which is written, "I believed, and therefore I spoke." We also believe, and therefore also we speak;

3709.text: knowing that he who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also with Jesus, and will present us with you.

3710.text: For all things are for your sakes, that the grace, being multiplied through the many, may cause the thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God.

3711.text: Therefore we do not faint, but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day.

3712.text: For our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory;

3713.text: while we do not look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.

3714.text: For we know that if the earthly house of our tent is dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal, in the heavens.

3715.text: For truly in this we groan, longing to be clothed with our habitation which is from heaven;

3716.text: if so be that being clothed we will not be found naked.

3717.text: For indeed we who are in this tent do groan, being burdened; not that we desire to be unclothed, but that we desire to be clothed, that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.

3718.text: Now he who made us for this very thing is God, who also gave to us the down payment of the Spirit.

3719.text: Therefore, we are always confident and know that while we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord;

3720.text: for we walk by faith, not by sight.

3721.text: We are of good courage, I say, and are willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be at home with the Lord.

3722.text: Therefore also we make it our aim, whether at home or absent, to be well pleasing to him.

3723.text: For we must all be revealed before the judgment seat of Christ; that each one may receive the things in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad.

3724.text: Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, but we are revealed to God; and I hope that we are revealed also in your consciences.

3725.text: For we are not commending ourselves to you again, but speak as giving you occasion of boasting on our behalf, that you may have something to answer those who boast in appearance, and not in heart.

3726.text: For if we are beside ourselves, it is for God. Or if we are of sober mind, it is for you.

3727.text: For the love of Christ constrains us; because we judge thus, that one died for all, therefore all died.

3728.text: He died for all, that those who live should no longer live to themselves, but to him who for their sakes died and rose again.

3729.text: Therefore we know no one after the flesh from now on. Even though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now we know him so no more.

3730.text: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, new things have come.

3731.text: But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation;

3732.text: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.

3733.text: We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beg you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.

3734.text: For him who knew no sin he made to be sin on our behalf; so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

3735.text: Working together, we entreat also that you not receive the grace of God in vain,

3736.text: for he says, "At an acceptable time I listened to you, in a day of salvation I helped you." Behold, now is the acceptable time. Behold, now is the day of salvation.

3737.text: We give no occasion of stumbling in anything, that our service may not be blamed,

3738.text: but in everything commending ourselves, as servants of God, in great endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses,

3739.text: in beatings, in imprisonments, in riots, in labors, in watchings, in fastings;

3740.text: in pureness, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in sincere love,

3741.text: in the word of truth, in the power of God; by the armor of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,

3742.text: by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report; as deceivers, and yet true;

3743.text: as unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and behold, we live; as punished, and not killed;

3744.text: as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.

3745.text: Our mouth is open to you, Corinthians. Our heart is enlarged.

3746.text: You are not restricted by us, but you are restricted by your own affections.

3747.text: Now in return, I speak as to my children, you also be open wide.

3748.text: Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers, for what fellowship have righteousness and iniquity? Or what fellowship has light with darkness?

3749.text: What agreement has Christ with Belial? Or what portion has a believer with an unbeliever?

3750.text: What agreement has a temple of God with idols? For we are a temple of the living God. Even as God said, "I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they will be my people."

3751.text: Therefore, "'Come out from among them, and be separate,' says the Lord. 'Touch no unclean thing. I will receive you.

3752.text: I will be to you a Father. You will be to me sons and daughters,' says the Lord Almighty."

3753.text: Having therefore these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

3754.text: Open your hearts to us. We wronged no one. We corrupted no one. We took advantage of no one.

3755.text: I say this not to condemn you, for I have said before, that you are in our hearts to die together and live together.

3756.text: Great is my boldness of speech toward you. Great is my boasting on your behalf. I am filled with comfort. I overflow with joy in all our affliction.

3757.text: For even when we had come into Macedonia, our flesh had no relief, but we were afflicted on every side. Fightings were outside. Fear was inside.

3758.text: Nevertheless, he who comforts the lowly, God, comforted us by the coming of Titus;

3759.text: and not by his coming only, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted in you, while he told us of your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me; so that I rejoiced still more.

3760.text: For though I made you sorry with my letter, I do not regret it, though I did regret it. For I see that my letter made you sorry, though just for a while.

3761.text: I now rejoice, not that you were made sorry, but that you were made sorry to repentance. For you were made sorry in a godly way, that you might suffer loss by us in nothing.

3762.text: For godly sorrow works repentance to salvation, which brings no regret. But the sorrow of the world works death.
